text: Getting promoted is way harder if you're not good in telling stories and rallying the team behind the shared goal and all these kind of things, and you usually achieve this through good storytelling techniques.
speaker: Petra Wille
context: Lenny asks Petra about the importance of storytelling and public speaking skills for product managers. Petra explains that while you can do IC-level product management work without strong storytelling abilities, it becomes a significant barrier to career advancement. She notes that getting promoted requires rallying teams around shared goals, which is primarily achieved through effective storytelling techniques.
text_ko: 스토리텔링을 잘하지 못하고 팀을 같은 목표로 모으는 데 능숙하지 않으면 승진이 훨씬 어려워요. 보통은 좋은 스토리텔링 기법(storytelling techniques)으로 그걸 해내요.
text_zh: 想升职，如果你讲不好故事、又带不动团队朝同一个目标努力，那就难多了。大多数情况下，这靠的是讲好故事的技巧（storytelling techniques）。
text_es: Conseguir un ascenso es mucho más difícil si no sabes contar historias ni movilizar al equipo en torno a un objetivo compartido; normalmente eso se logra con buenas técnicas de narración (storytelling).
key_sentence: Getting promoted is harder without decent storytelling and rallying the team.
original_text: Getting promoted is way harder if you're not good in telling stories and rallying the team behind the shared goal and all these kind of things, and you usually achieve this through good storytelling techniques. And in some teams, I've seen the product person not being really, really good at it, but then the whole team helped creating these stories and stuff like this. So you definitely could compensate to some extent, but I would consider it a bit of a career staller if you don't get to a decent level of storytelling and to a decent level of public speaking.

vocabulary.definition: Methods and strategies used to convey a narrative effectively, engaging an audience and enhancing understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, storytelling techniques are employed to communicate ideas, values, and visions in a compelling manner, often during presentations or marketing campaigns.
vocabulary.nuance: This term implies a creative approach to communication, suggesting that effective storytelling goes beyond mere facts to evoke emotions and connections.

vocabulary.definition: The act of motivating and uniting a group of individuals towards a common purpose or objective.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate setting, rallying the team is crucial for fostering collaboration and ensuring that all members are aligned with the company's goals, especially during challenging times.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase carries a connotation of enthusiasm and urgency, often used in contexts where morale needs boosting or direction is required.

vocabulary.definition: An objective or aim that is collectively pursued by a group or organization, fostering collaboration and teamwork.
vocabulary.businessContext: Establishing a shared goal is fundamental in business environments, as it ensures that all team members are working towards the same outcome, enhancing productivity and cohesion.
vocabulary.nuance: This term emphasizes collective effort and mutual investment, suggesting that individual contributions are directed towards a common purpose.

text: One thing that has made me sense out the most is I see product people on the IC level have to go through some of the struggles on their own, even if our product community has some best practices to it.
speaker: Petra Wille
context: Lenny asks what non-product people who lead product teams lack most in terms of understanding product management. Petra explains that managers from other backgrounds often don't understand the product management craft or community, so they can't guide their product people toward existing solutions and resources. This forces individual contributor product managers to learn everything on their own instead of being directed to established best practices and learning materials.
text_ko: 제가 가장 크게 느낀 건 개인 기여자(Individual Contributor, IC) 위치에 있는 프로덕트 담당자(product people)들이 우리 프로덕트 커뮤니티에 모범 사례(best practices)가 있더라도 여전히 어떤 어려움은 혼자서 겪어야 한다는 점이에요.
text_zh: 让我最有感触的是，我发现处在个人贡献者（IC level）的产品人，很多时候得自己扛一些难题，哪怕我们产品社区里已经有一些最佳实践 (best practices)。
text_es: Algo que me ha quedado claro es que la gente de producto a nivel de IC (Individual Contributor) tiene que afrontar algunas de las dificultades por su cuenta, aunque en nuestra comunidad de producto sí hay buenas prácticas (best practices).
key_sentence: product people on the IC level have to go through some of the struggles on their own
original_text: One thing that has made me sense out the most is I see product people on the IC level have to go through some of the struggles on their own, even if our product community has some best practices to it. Because as the line manager has no clue about the product community out there and the craftless product management, they often struggle to point them in the right direction to say, 'Hey, I think that's a problem somebody else already had. So maybe you could watch a talk or read this blog post or there's a book about this particular thing and then go try it.'

vocabulary.definition: Best practices refer to the most efficient and effective methods or techniques that have been established through experience and research.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, best practices are often documented guidelines that teams follow to optimize processes and improve outcomes.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a level of consensus and proven success, making it more authoritative than simply 'good practices.'

vocabulary.definition: Struggles refer to challenges or difficulties faced in achieving a goal or overcoming obstacles.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of product development, struggles may involve technical issues, resource constraints, or market competition that impede progress.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often conveys a sense of effort and perseverance, suggesting that overcoming these challenges is a part of the growth process.

vocabulary.definition: Community refers to a group of individuals who share common interests, goals, or values, often interacting and supporting each other.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business or tech context, a community can consist of users, developers, or stakeholders who collaborate and share knowledge to enhance a product or service.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a sense of belonging and mutual support, which can be crucial for fostering innovation and engagement.

text: Then step number two is having a clear idea where every PM currently is in their current career, in their situation, life in general, all these kind of things.
speaker: Petra Wille
context: Lenny asks Petra about her five ingredients for coaching product managers effectively. Petra is explaining the second ingredient, which involves assessing where each PM currently stands and creating a vision for their development. She emphasizes that product leaders should think beyond just the current role and company when envisioning their team member's growth potential, and focus on identifying the next meaningful challenge that would help them develop new skills.
text_ko: 두 번째 단계는 각 프로덕트 매니저(PM)가 지금 경력상 어디에 있고, 개인적인 상황이나 삶 전반은 어떤지를 명확히 파악하는 거예요.
text_zh: 第二步就是要搞清楚每个产品经理 (PM) 现在在职业发展、个人处境和生活上到底处在哪儿。
text_es: El segundo paso es saber exactamente en qué punto se encuentra cada gerente de producto (product manager/PM): en su carrera profesional, en su situación personal y en la vida en general.
key_sentence: having a clear idea where every PM currently is in their current career
original_text: Then step number two is having a clear idea where every PM currently is in their current career, in their situation, life in general, all these kind of things. So put the pin on the map, so to say, and then think about what is your vision for them in the future, so how good could it get? And I usually encourage product leads to think bigger than their current role at the current company because that's the longer term thing. And then even more important is what I call the next bigger challenge.

vocabulary.definition: A well-defined and unambiguous understanding or concept of a particular subject or situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, having a clear idea is crucial for strategic planning, decision-making, and aligning team objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'clear idea' suggests clarity and precision, it can imply a lack of flexibility or openness to alternative perspectives.

vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'currently' is often used to describe the present status of projects, market conditions, or employee roles.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'currently' emphasizes the temporal aspect and may imply that the situation could change in the future.

vocabulary.definition: A set of circumstances or state of affairs in which one finds oneself.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding the current situation is vital for effective problem-solving, strategic planning, and resource allocation.
vocabulary.nuance: The word 'situation' can carry a neutral tone, but it may also imply complexity or difficulty, depending on the context.

text: First of all, people that's starting, often they are getting a better storytelling journey. Often totally underestimate how many time actually great storytellers are investing in creating the stories and making sure they can share the story in nice ways and formats.
speaker: Petra Wille
context: Lenny asks Petra for concrete advice on how product managers can become better storytellers. Petra explains that people beginning their storytelling improvement journey often don't realize how much time and effort great storytellers invest in crafting their stories. She emphasizes that creating compelling stories requires significant preparation and iteration, not just natural talent or quick improvisation.
text_ko: 무엇보다도, 처음 시작하는 사람들은 보통 자신의 스토리텔링(storytelling)이 꽤 잘 되고 있다고 생각하는 경우가 많아요. 그런데 진짜 훌륭한 스토리텔러들이 이야기를 만들어내고, 보기 좋은 방식과 여러 형식(formats)으로 잘 전달할 수 있게 얼마나 많은 시간을 투자하는지 대개 과소평가해요.
text_zh: 先说，刚开始的人常常觉得自己在讲故事（storytelling）上进展很快。但他们往往完全低估了真正会讲故事的人到底投入了多少时间去打磨内容，并确保能用更吸引人的方式和合适的格式把故事呈现出来。
text_es: Para empezar, quienes están empezando suelen creer que ya tienen una buena narrativa (storytelling). Subestiman cuánto tiempo invierten en realidad los grandes narradores (storytellers) en crear las historias y en asegurarse de que se puedan compartir de forma atractiva y en los formatos adecuados.
key_sentence: Often totally underestimate how many time actually great storytellers are investing in creating the stories
original_text: First of all, people that's starting, often they are getting a better storytelling journey. Often totally underestimate how many time actually great storytellers are investing in creating the stories and making sure they can share the story in nice ways and formats. So that's maybe the first tip, you have to plan to put in a lot of work to create your story.

vocabulary.definition: The art of conveying events, experiences, or ideas through narrative techniques to engage an audience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, storytelling is often used in marketing and branding to create emotional connections with customers and convey a company's values or mission effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: While storytelling can evoke strong emotions, it is important to ensure that the narrative is authentic and aligns with the brand's identity.

vocabulary.definition: The act of allocating resources, usually money, into an asset or project with the expectation of generating a return or profit.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, investing often refers to venture capital funding, where investors provide capital to early-stage companies in exchange for equity.
vocabulary.nuance: Investing implies a level of risk and requires careful analysis and strategy to maximize potential returns.

vocabulary.definition: The arrangement or structure in which information is presented or conveyed.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, formats can refer to various types of media used for communication, such as reports, presentations, or digital content, which can impact how the message is received.
vocabulary.nuance: Choosing the right format is crucial, as it can enhance clarity and engagement, while a poor choice may lead to misunderstandings.

vocabulary.definition: The process or experience of traveling from one point to another, often used metaphorically to describe personal or professional growth.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the term 'customer journey' refers to the complete experience a customer has with a brand, from initial awareness to post-purchase interactions.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a series of stages or steps, highlighting the importance of each phase in achieving overall success.

text: And then the other tip would be really make sure that you're using language that speaks to the heart and the minds of the people because we constantly tend to use too much of our business lingo and it's banner blindness.
speaker: Petra Wille
context: Lenny asks for concrete storytelling advice for product managers. Petra explains that effective storytelling requires using natural, emotional language rather than business jargon. She introduces the concept of "banner blindness" - when audiences tune out overused corporate terms. She suggests that even established product management terminology like "product discovery" might need to be replaced with simpler, more relatable language if teams have become desensitized to it.
text_ko: 그리고 또 한 가지 팁은 사람들의 마음과 생각에 직접 와 닿는 표현을 쓰고 있는지 꼭 확인하세요. 우리는 자꾸 비즈니스 용어를 너무 많이 써서 사람들이 무시해 버리는 경향이 있고, 결국 배너 블라인드니스(banner blindness)가 생겨요.
text_zh: 还有一个建议：一定要用能打动人心、触及受众思维的语言。我们老是太爱用自己的业务行话，结果大家对那些东西都麻木了，形成了广告盲区（banner blindness）。
text_es: Y otra recomendación: asegúrate de usar un lenguaje que conecte con el corazón y la mente de las personas; tendemos a abusar de la jerga empresarial y eso provoca ceguera ante los banners (banner blindness).
key_sentence: Use language that speaks to the heart and minds to avoid banner blindness.
original_text: And then the other tip would be really make sure that you're using language that speaks to the heart and the minds of the people because we constantly tend to use too much of our business lingo and it's banner blindness. Some of the words that we're using people totally overhearing them because we're using them so often. And it could be even things like product discovery. So maybe your company is already so fed up with all your product discovery stuff that you should start using different terms.

vocabulary.definition: A phenomenon where users consciously or unconsciously ignore banner-like information on websites or applications, often due to overexposure.
vocabulary.businessContext: In digital marketing, banner blindness can significantly reduce the effectiveness of online advertising, necessitating more engaging and innovative approaches to capture audience attention.
vocabulary.nuance: Understanding banner blindness is crucial for marketers to design ads that stand out and resonate with users, rather than blending into the background.

text: For example, I found that oftentimes there is a bit of a community of practice internally, but they never heard about external product community.
speaker: Petra Wille
context: Lenny asks about Petra's research into product management communities and their value. Petra explains her survey findings about how many product managers are unaware of external communities like Lenny's community, Teresa Torres' community, or Mind the Product. She finds this surprising given how willing people in the product community are to share knowledge and help others avoid repeating the same mistakes and challenges.
text_ko: 예를 들어, 제가 보니 내부에는 일종의 실무 커뮤니티(community of practice)가 있긴 한데, 외부의 제품 커뮤니티(product community)에 대해서는 전혀 들어본 적이 없더라고요.
text_zh: 比如，我发现很多时候，内部有点儿像一个实践共同体 (community of practice)，但他们根本没听说过外部的产品社群 (external product community)。
text_es: Por ejemplo, he visto que a menudo hay una comunidad de práctica (community of practice) interna, pero que nunca han oído hablar de la comunidad de producto (product community) externa.
key_sentence: they never heard about external product community.
original_text: For example, I found that oftentimes there is a bit of a community of practice internally, but they never heard about external product community. So they never heard of your community or to raise this community or mind the product or any of those external communities. And that is shocking to an extent as well because we're all so friendly human beings, happy to share what we learn, and they don't have to go through the same things over and over again.

vocabulary.definition: A group of individuals who share a common interest or profession and engage in collective learning through regular interaction and collaboration.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, communities of practice facilitate knowledge sharing and innovation among employees, often leading to improved practices and solutions within an organization.
vocabulary.nuance: This term emphasizes the collaborative and informal nature of learning, making it suitable for contexts where peer-to-peer engagement is valued over formal training.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to or located on the outside; in business, it refers to factors, stakeholders, or entities that exist outside of an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding external factors, such as market trends or customer feedback, is crucial for businesses to adapt strategies and remain competitive.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'external' can imply a broader perspective, it may also suggest a lack of direct control or influence over those factors.
